title: Riska’s Study Time
text: The next time Itsuki came to his senses… he was apparently inside a slave trader’s cage, I say.
“W-where… am I…?”
Itsuki apparently shot upright, only to nearly writhe in agony from the pain in the back of his head. And it seemed his wrists and ankles had been fitted with manacles and shackles.
“Where on earth… is this place!?”
“Oh? Looks like you’re awake.”
The one who called out to Itsuki as he lay sprawled in the cage was, apparently, the slave trader—a different person from the monster dealer we knew, it seemed.
“You got sold off as a slave, you filthy Beastman…”
“Wha—! What in the world does that mean! Just who would do such a thing as sell me!”

“Ain’t my job to go blabbing about the customer to the merchandise. Dunno what the deal is, but you’re a weird Beastman we can’t put a slave crest on—though that don’t mean we can’t still sell you. Oi.”
“Yes, sir!”
“Wait, I still have more to say—stop— mmph—”

Right about there, the now-fully-awake Itsuki was nearly fitted with a gag. The reason a slave crest couldn’t be applied was, of course, the power of the weapon. Naturally that applied to Father, myself, and Itsuki, and Ren too—though in this particular loop, Wolf had also had his slave crest removed. In any case, judging from the sequence of events and the present circumstantial evidence, it was obvious that Smoked Meat and his lot had knocked Itsuki out and sold him straight to the slave trader.
Itsuki apparently tried to reflexively begin chanting a spell.
“Whoa, seems like this one can use magic.”
“Like hell I’ll let you!”
He got kicked square in the gut and, writhing in pain, his spell was interrupted.
“Oi. Fetch the restraints for slaves who can use magic! Damn it, if the slave crest actually worked we wouldn’t need this junk.”
And so, Itsuki was fitted with restraints designed to prevent him from using magic.

“How thoughtful of you, carrying around some cursed bow you can’t take off… weird slave, this one. Said something about being the sinful lowlife impersonating the Bow Hero, huh? Ha, taking the cosplay real seriously, ain’t he.”

From there, with his mouth silenced and manacles, shackles, and even weights added on, Itsuki was forced into the full slave experience, it seemed. For a while he was left lying in the slave trader’s cage. His Level fell just barely short of what was needed to use the Portal Skill, leaving him trapped with no way to flee.

He apparently tried to resist by moving the bow somehow, but the manacles made it hard to draw properly. Even so, determined to use whatever he could, he apparently used his tail to draw an arrow and fight back. Of course, they saw through his aim and beat him senseless for it. Eventually, Itsuki was purchased by a noble for the purpose of torture.
“C’mon! Cry louder! Hahahahaha!”

Strung up by both wrists in an underground dungeon, he was subjected to whipping, of course, as well as being beaten in the stomach and face with blunt weapons. By that point they’d fitted him with a collar that choked tightly around his neck whenever he tried to chant a spell, and the torture continued on.
“Aaaaagh!? Guh… st-stop— h-help me—”
Even when the pain finally became too much and he lost consciousness, they doused him with water to force him back awake, torturing him until he wept and screamed once more.
“Hii, aaaahhh… st-stop it…”
There were apparently other slaves in that same cell, but Itsuki said he never got a good look at their faces.
“Doing something like this… even if the nation permits it… I— justice would never allow it…”
“Ha! Listen to this one. Justice belongs to us humans. It has no business belonging to you filthy Beastmen!”
“Ngh—”
“There’s no god for slaves!”

Even so, Itsuki swore in his heart that justice would surely be carried out, that once he escaped this place he would mete out a punishment fitting for this noble. A boiling rage was rising up from the very depths of his body. Whose fault was it that he was suffering such an unreasonable fate? Usa-unny’s? The companions who hadn’t believed him even after he’d explained everything, and sold him off instead? Or the slave trader who’d bought him? The noble torturing him? The nation that decreed all Demi-Humans and Beastmen were evil? He felt his bow throb—thud, thud—like a heartbeat. The conditions for the Curse Series bow had been unlocked. He could feel a pitch-black emotion bubbling up from the depths of his soul.
“Guuuuh… I will never forgive any of you.”
“This one just never learns to shut up. Oi.”
“Yes, sir!”

And so, Itsuki apparently found himself bound hand and foot to a table, laid flat. His tail was stretched out and restrained, and the noble who’d purchased him produced a saw, seemingly for the express purpose of showing it off to him.
“It’s that defiant attitude of yours that’s the problem. You really must be properly punished for it, mustn’t you?”
And with that, the noble, overflowing with sadistic delight, began drawing the saw back and forth—slowly, deliberately—across Itsuki’s outstretched tail.
“Wha— what are you planning to do! S-stop it! Stop— iiiggghhh… aaaaaahhhh”

The noble dragged the saw’s blade across Itsuki’s tail again and again, seemingly to maximize his suffering. Naturally, the pain was excruciating and the blood flowed, staining the blade red. Eventually, with a wet snap, the tail was severed clean through. While listening to this account, Father had gone pale, his face contorted as though he couldn’t bear to hear another word. Still, he didn’t make Itsuki stop, since Itsuki himself kept talking.
“Aaaaaaaaaahhhh! Aaaaahhh…”

Itsuki apparently had his own severed tail placed right in front of him while he writhed in agony. Though it was a tail that wouldn’t have existed at all had he not become a Riska, having a part of yourself severed off still brings on a tremendous sense of loss, I say. His rage went quiet, and despair spread out before him instead, or so he described it.
“There, now do you understand your place? If you still don’t get it, I won’t go easy on you until I show you an even more painful time, understand?”

Amid that despair, all Itsuki could do was sit there hollow and lifeless, like a broken husk. Why, why was this happening to him… At first, the thought that it was all Usa-unny’s fault had surfaced in his mind, but gradually, as his thinking became stained through and through with rage, he began to realize that the true cause wasn’t Usa-unny at all, but rather Smoked Meat and the rest, and this whole rotten nation. Even so, there was nothing he could do in his current state, and he cursed himself fiercely for being bound and helpless.
“Th-this is… what in the world is going on here!”
In the midst of that situation, whether Itsuki’s screams had reached her or not, a young girl entered the room, and upon seeing Itsuki being tortured, she raised her voice.

“Well, well, if it isn’t Miss Ivyred. What do you mean, what’s going on? I’m simply teaching this slave its place. If you’re to be a noble of this nation too, it’s important you learn to appreciate such refinements. It’s because creatures like these exist that the world can’t know peace.”
“Even if he is a slave, this kind of act is wrong! I’ll report this to the crown!”
“Miss Ivyred, you truly don’t seem to understand your own position. Your parents, a poor noble family, came here to serve, did they not? Doing something like this will only bring your parents grief.”
“Fweh… no, Papa and Mama would forgive me for this! This is wrong! Torture like this is forbidden under this nation’s laws!”
“Honestly… how deplorable, both parent and child alike. Oi. Take this girl who doesn’t know her place to another room.”
“Fweeeeh! Mister Beastman! Fweeeeeeh!”

The girl, who appeared to be a maid and had raised her voice in protest, was seized at the noble’s subordinate’s command and dragged off somewhere, and all Itsuki could do, his consciousness hazy, was watch her go. Ah… there was still someone out there who’d mustered the courage to try to save him. He was still all right; he mustn’t let himself go mad—so said a faint sliver of belief that remained, clinging to Riska’s words, or something along those lines, Itsuki mused, his gaze distant as if steeped in memory, seemingly lost in it. And there, apparently, his consciousness faded away.
